A critical obligation under the MHSA is the employer's duty to conduct comprehensive hazard identification and risk assessments (HIRAs) for all work processes. For a drill-and-blast contractor, this means a detailed, documented analysis of every potential risk, from the stability of the drill rig and the handling of explosives to the dangers of fly-rock, misfires, and post-blast fumes. Based on this assessment, the contractor must develop and implement a robust Safety Management System (SMS), including codes of practice (COPs) for all high-risk activities. Furthermore, the MHSA mandates a series of legal appointments, where competent individuals are given legal responsibility for specific aspects of health and safety. For a contractor like Veralogix, this would include appointing a senior manager as the legally responsible person (often termed a Section 4.4 appointee) for the contract work, who can be held personally accountable for any contraventions of the Act.
